message.reasoning:
I need to make a Monopoly decision.

I have $382 and am on St. Charles Place with one Get Out of Jail Free card. My pink and orange monopolies are fully developed, but my light blue properties remain mortgaged. Player two has $395 and is on Pennsylvania Avenue with a mortgaged rail road and a red monopoly.

Player three is bankrupt. Player four has $276 and is on the Reading Railroad with a mortgaged yellow monopoly. The bank has no houses left. The housing lock is the key asset.

I will not build hotels. Hotels return four houses to the bank, which player two could use to complete his red monopoly. I will not unmortgage light blue properties or sell houses unless in debt. I will not trade orange, pink, or Get Out of Jail Free cards. My $382 cash is just above the $360 rent on Marvin Gardens two houses. Unmortgaging anything would drop me below that buffer.

Hotel upgrades cost $100 each. Player two has $395 and could buy the returned houses to complete his red monopoly. That would raise my rent to $950–$1000 while making his reds far more dangerous.

Player two’s red monopoly would rise to $875–$1100 if completed. Player four could buy a yellow house for $150 and raise Marvin Gardens from two to three houses, forcing $800 rent that would bankrupt me. I will not build hotels.

Unmortgaging all three light blues would cost $154 and leave me with $228. That is below the $360 rent on Marvin Gardens. Unmortgaging Short Line alone would cost $110 and leave me with $272. That is also below the $360 rent. I will not unmortgage any light blue properties.

Player four has roughly $300 in house equity from his yellow monopoly. He could liquidate it to pay rent or buy houses.

Player four’s total liquidation is roughly $606. That covers the $750 rent on orange four houses, but not the $800 rent. He cannot survive both orange rents without mortgaging more.

Player four has no unmortgaged properties left, so he cannot pay the $750 or $800 rent on orange four houses. He would go bankrupt if he lands there. I am double-checking the standard Monopoly rent chart for pink two-house properties.

Standard Monopoly rent for pink two-house properties is $200–$220, not the $180 I had assumed. Virginia Avenue at two houses is $220. The standard yellow rent on Marvin Gardens at two houses is $360, which matches my earlier figure. However, standard yellow at three houses is $850, not $800.
